name: Anti-Signal Recognition Particle (SRP) Myopathy

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: European Neuromuscular Centre (ENMC) 2016 Criteria for Immune-Mediated Necrotizing Myopathy

criteria.description: Presence of anti-SRP autoantibodies in serum
Severe proximal muscle weakness, often rapidly progressive
Muscle biopsy showing necrotizing myopathy with minimal inflammatory infiltrate
Markedly elevated serum creatine kinase (CK) levels

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of anti-SRP autoantibodies plus clinical evidence of proximal muscle weakness and muscle biopsy consistent with necrotizing myopathy
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Exclusion of other myopathies and inflammatory myositis is essential

pathognomonic.notes: Typically affects shoulder and hip girdle muscles

common.notes: Often >10 times upper limit of normal
Due to involvement of oropharyngeal muscles

rare.notes: Less common than in other inflammatory myopathies

laboratory: Elevated serum creatine kinase (CK) often >10x normal
Positive anti-SRP autoantibodies detected by immunoassay
imaging: Muscle MRI showing muscle edema and fatty replacement
Chest imaging to evaluate for interstitial lung disease if suspected
genetic: No known genetic mutations; disease is autoimmune in nature
other: Muscle biopsy demonstrating necrotizing myopathy with minimal inflammatory infiltrate
Electromyography showing myopathic motor unit potentials

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of anti-HMGCR antibodies instead of anti-SRP
Muscle biopsy similar but clinical context differs
More prominent inflammatory infiltrates on muscle biopsy
Distal muscle involvement and finger flexor weakness
Presence of rimmed vacuoles on muscle biopsy

redFlags: Rapidly progressive muscle weakness leading to respiratory failure
Dysphagia with risk of aspiration pneumonia
references: Allenbach Y, et al. Anti-SRP autoantibody-associated necrotizing myopathy: clinical features and outcome in 100 patients. Arthritis Rheumatol. 2016.
European Neuromuscular Centre (ENMC) International Workshop: Classification of Idiopathic Inflammatory Myopathies. Neuromuscul Disord. 2016.
Lloyd TE, et al. Immune-mediated necrotizing myopathy: clinical features and treatment outcomes. Muscle Nerve. 2020.
